title: Bind the order-search query parameters to the types callers ask for

blocks.text: The order-search endpoint reads its query string into a map, and every handler gets its parameters through `QueryParam`, as in `QueryParam.PAGE.get(query, Integer.class)`. The binding layer that fills a handler's arguments is generic code that passes the result on as an `Object`. Last week a handler declared its `limit` argument as a `String`. The request passed the binding layer, and the error turned up two services away, in a report job that read the stored value back.
Parsing already works. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/QueryParam.java`:

items: `get(...)`: hand the parsed value back as the type the caller asked for;
`boxed(...)`: the class whose instances a caller asking for `type` can be given.

blocks.text: When you're done, a caller that asks for a type the parameter doesn't hold gets a `ClassCastException` from `get` itself, while callers that ask for `int`, `boolean`, or a wider type such as `Number` get their value. About four lines in total.

cases.says: each parameter comes back as the type its value has, and a parameter the query lacks comes back as null
a request for a type the parameter's value doesn't have fails with ClassCastException inside get, even when the caller's own code checks nothing
a caller may ask for int or boolean and gets the value
a caller may ask for a supertype of the value's type, such as Number for an Integer

origin.section: A `Class<T>` Token Makes the Cast Real, Inside the Method

concepts: Casting with a Class<T> token makes a wrong request fail inside the method, and accepts any supertype of the value's class.
A primitive token such as int.class accepts no object, so it must be mapped to its wrapper; a token can't name a parameterized type.
